info.title: passalong-server API
info.summary: The contract between passalong-server and the passalong client.
info.description: Version 1 of the contract, as passalong-server v0.1.0 serves it. REST + JSON; item content travels as byte streams. The server never interprets an item's `meta` and never exposes a field taken from it. Every request is safe to repeat: each operation that is not a GET says in `x-passalong-replay` what the same request, sent again, is answered. `x-passalong-errors` lists the codes an operation can refuse with. See README.md and rewrite-session.md beside this file.

apiKey.description: The key selects the workspace; no request names one.

ItemId.description: `<creation time>-<content key>`, as in the passalong client's item schema. Proposed by the client; parsed strictly.

KeyId.description: The id of a workspace's data key. The server compares key ids and never sees a key.

UploadId.description: An upload's id, and its idempotency key.

Bytes.description: A byte count, as a string: item sizes are 64-bit and JSON numbers are not.

Opaque.description: A document the client wrote and the server never looks into.

Item.description: The envelope: what the server knows of an item. `meta` is the client's `meta.json`, byte for byte.

created.description: `false` when identical content was stored already.

expectedKeyId.description: The current key id; null for the plaintext workspace a migration starts from.

holder.description: The public id of the API key that holds the lease.

newHeader.description: The header `beginRewrite` brought: the new data key, wrapped under the new words, which the workspace gets on commit. Whoever resumes the session, the holder after a restart or another device after `takeOverRewrite`, unlocks it with the new words. `Encryption.header` stays the old one until the commit, because that is what opens the items readers get. Added after the first draft of v1.

keyId.description: While a rewrite is open: still the key readers need, the one before it.

maxItemBytes.description: null: no limit. The client checks it before it uploads, because its other backends have none.

sourceUrl.description: Where the source of this server is. The server is AGPL-3.0-or-later: whoever runs a modified one for others must offer them its source, and points this at it. Added after the first draft of v1; a client must not require it.

Problem.description: RFC 9457 problem details, with a stable `code`.
